description:

reviewText: This sonic cleaner is a great addition to my Jewel Jet Steam Cleaner. Not that I needed an additional cleaning, I used this in place of my soaking for 30 seconds routine before I steam. So I place it in here and then rinse dry and steam. This comes out very nice, and when I am in a rush, I just toss it in here and get my jewelry clean. I use this is Connesuiers *maybe spelled wrong* LeSonic Concentrate cleaner. I will try Blitz next time from my Jeweler.Back to the product, it is good, it is an additive and is okay to be used alone but you won't get the same effects from the Jeweler. I do, because I use all, Sonic Cleaner, Steamer and polisher. So my ring is better than when they just take it and steam or sonic clean it. BUt not as good as when I have to leave it over night for a real treat. LOL, but to get that we need other tools. I am pleased, yet I expected more. People said dirt was in there after cleaning their ring, mines was not the case. Don't know if it is because I clean my ring almost every day. Or If it just isn't that great. I placed my watch in there it had some scum on it, and while some seemed to have softened it didn't come off. BOO HOO I didn't like that. I give it five stars because I didn't want it to do my total cleaning. Yet, if I am in a rush it does that just fine. I enjoy using it with my Steamer which is what I bought if for. It is very affordable I paid $30. I haven't tried glasses will try my shades. description:

reviewText: I bought this bag for a daily commute bag to carry my laptop and files.  The bag is in a very attractive shade of medium classic red with white stitching and pretty buckles.  It is also very spacious and can fit much in its main compartment. There is a vintage feel to the leather.  It is not smooth and buttery like Coach's glove tanned leather nor is it soft but thin like cheap leather.  It is relatively thick and feels more artisanal and less mass-produced.Here are my issues with this bag:- No organization feature - The front pocket under the two buckles does not have any zippers so you can only put things in there that you don't care too much if they slip out and are lost.  There is only one small inside pocket to put my wallet.  I must put my other small items - Blackberry & pens, etc. in the large compartment.  It is very challenging to locate these items once the bag is full of files and such.- Flimsy and not adjustable strap - The included strap is quite thin and you cannot adjust its length.  It really would have been better to make the handles a bit longer so I can just carry the bag by the handles and not use the strap all-together.This is a pretty bag with European flair.  However, it is not the ideal commute bag due to the lack of organization features and the flimsy strap.  It probably would be better to use this bag as an overnight bag than an everyday commute bag.
summary: Nice leather, good size but no organization feature

title: Maxpedition Rollypoly Extreme Backpack
description: The #0233 ROLLYPOLY EXTREME is a radical evolution of Maxpedition’s unique sequential folding pouch concept.
reviewText: I wanted a fold-up bag to take with us when we go on a cruise. There are not a lot of fold-ups out there, and most of them left a lot to be desired. This is probably an exception to most bags of this type.The bag does look a bit military, but after spending my time in the military, I have no desire to play G.I. Joe. However, the bag fulfills a purpose, which is why I purchased it.This bag is well made, which is unusual in the roll-up category, as most bags of this type are pretty cheap. But you pay a premium price for the quality - but that is normal in life. Hefty YKK zippers are used on this bag, as well as double-stitching throughout. And there are 7 different compartments in the bag.It folds up into a round package, about 4.5" Dia x 6" or so. In the folded state, you could attach it to a belt or backpack, but I have found that packing it flat in my luggage works better. It lays flat in the front compartment of my suitcase. There is no padding in a backpack of this type, but the good news is when packed flat, it takes up no more room than a t-shirt.Fully opened and laid out flat, its about 17" high x 14" or so. It reminds me more of a tote bag in style than a bona-fide backpack, as its only about 1" or so deep when laid out flat.What is unusual about this bag is it has room for a 70oz water bladder (a 100oz bladder won't fit). While it might be argued that having to pack a water bladder in your suitcase might defeat the idea of a roll-up, it can nevertheless work for this purpose. There are even elastic strips on the harness to hold the tube of the bladder.The main compartment has a divider to separate the bladder from the other items, and there is a drain hole at the bottom on each side of the divider. The main compartment will easily hold two beach towels and the bladder.  There are also two separate compartments on the front of the bag that are large enough to hold sunscreen, sunglasses, a hard-cover book, and a few other items.Another unusual feature for a roll-up backpack is that it has a sternum strap, and even a whistle built-into the buckle.The top load flap is rather unusual. The top cover is only about 1/3rd of the bag's width, and the straps cover the rest of the opening. While this is not a waterproof enclosure, you won't likely be going to the beach when it's raining anyway.One word to the wise however, if you are taking this bag on a cruise, that in some countries it's illegal to wear camouflage pattern clothing. Unlike many of Maxpedition products, this item is not available in camouflage, but it is available in khaki and OD Green. However, to be safe, I always buy items I am taking abroad in black.All in all, its the perfect bag to take to the pool, the beach, or on your excursion.Post Cruise Update:------------------------------------------------------------------------------After taking the backpack on our first cruise, we had one of the sternum straps fall off. They are intended to be removable I suppose, so you need to check them from time-to-time to make sure the straps do not work their way out of the buckles. If you want to permanently affix the sternum straps, you can double the ends of the webbing over and sew them, which will prevent the webbing from working its way out of the buckles.Also we carried a cold 32 oz bottle of water that we bought on board the ship on our way out for an excursion. Without having any insulation in the backpack, the bottle soon sweated due to the mid-80 deg temperature and humidity so that my back soon got wet. If you carry chilled water, you might want either an insulated bottle or an insulated sleeve if you purchase bottled water.But I don't really fault the backpack as it's not supposed to be insulated, which makes it fold up into a small package.We did find a rather useful feature of the top load flap. title: Tonto(TM) Concealed-Carry Mini-Messenger Bag w/ MOLLE by Hazard 4(R)
description: Sometimes a small bag is all you need, or all that fits in tight quarters. This is where your Sidekick(TM) Tonto(TM) shines. It has lots of organizational features, a rugged exterior, and modular expandability. It's also equipped with multiple concealed-carry areas, so it won't leave those who go into harm's way unprotected.
reviewText: I need to make two comments right at the start.  The first is to acknowledge ROSCOEBA for an excellant review of this product on YouTube.  It gave me a good idea of what this bag was capable of before I purchased it.My second comment is that I do not carry a concealed weapon.  So, I will not be speaking to that aspect of the bag.On to the review.I have gone though a number of bags in the past year.  I still have most of these items because each bag performs a specific function well.  However, I was unable to find the right bag that I could carry every day.  You see I need to carry a LOT of medical supplies for personal use.  There are a number of bags capable of handling my load out, but most are either lacking in internal organization; or the size and shape of the bag makes it unfit to work my other bags.  (i.e. a full loaded bag will not fit ino my Maxpedition Malage, which I use for carrying my laptop or iPad to the office.)What I wanted was something a little bigger (and better shaped) than a Condor Rip-Awa7 EMT bag.  The Maxpedition NeatFreak is about the right size, but the internal organization was inadequate, because most of the pocket any sort of closure.  Enter the Hazard 4 Tonto.  It is about the same size as the NeatFreak externally, but has a number of zippered compartments to better support my load-out.  My every day carry items consists of the following items.On my person: watch, wallet and keys.In the bag:Fron flap: diabetic supplies: insulin (in a cooler pouch), and glucose monitor w/supplies (in its own pouch).On the mole: Leatherman Freestyle and Vicroinox Ranger, each clipped to one of the two two-inch web straps.In the admin pouch: eyeglasses, in a case, portable magnifying glass, roll of hard candy, two bottles of eye drios, pen, doctor's medicatal instructions (folded), and instructions for the EMS team, in the map area.In the main compartment: an upper arm blood pressure monitor with some room left over for some packaged food items (granola bars, small jar of nuts, etc.)The back pouch holds my Kindle when I am going to the doctor's office.The side pouch holds my assortment of pills for the month.Finally, my cell phone is clipped to the other side of bag.The beautiful thing about this arrangement is that I only need to slip the entire bag (strap and all) into the Malag in order to complete my business EDC, which can include a 13 inch laptop (or iPad), a legal pad, and other sundry items.The Tonto carries well via the padded handle or via the shoulder strap.  I utilze both methods on a daily basis.  It is big enough to hold my daily supplies, but it is not cumbersome or bulky.  This is good because this bag is never out of reach.  There is also the benefit of the admin area which can serve as a tray when I need it.This is an excellent addition to my personal EDC system.  I should say that if you want a single bag that holds everything than the Tonto is not for you.  It won't hold a Kindle comfortable for instance.  It is also not a good choice if you need to carry unfolded sheets of paper with you all tihe time.  However, if you carry light, or you need a bag to fit into and extended EDC system (like me) then this may be the best fit for you.Before I end, I should speak to the quality of the construction and the type of service Hazard 4 provides.  The material is 1000 D Cordura.  This is softer and more compliant that the material Maxpedition uses.  I have a number of Maxpediton bags and really like their construction.  However, I appreciate the material that Hazard 4 is using as well.  It is softer, but seems just as durable.  I like the soft feel on this type of bag.  I'm not sure I would want the same material on the Malaga because it might cause a larger bag to sag.  I don't know for sure as I haven't seen a larger bag with this material - just saying.Regarding their service, I contacted the Hazard 4 help desk before I purchased the product.  They were both polite and replied promptly.Bottom line: if you need a small bag that has more flexibility than a Fatboy or Neatfreak; that is comfortable to carry (via handle or shoulder strap); and has a relatively low profile than your search has ended.  Get the Tonto.Hope this helps.

description: This durable backpack combines dedicated organization for the work week yet is roomy enough for a trip to the gym or the occasional weekend adventure.Rear organization compartment has an elevated laptop compartment for your 17 inch Macbook Pro(R), a sleeve for your iPad and plush lined pockets to store your cell phone or iPodAluminum hardware and water-resistant fabrics combine to create a lightweight, durable bagHeat-molded, crush proof SafeZone compartment protects your sunglasses, iPhone, portable electronics and other fragile gear
reviewText: This is the best backpack I have ever used in my entire life.The first thing you'll notice is how durable the materials are. This bag is SOLID. The zippers and buckles are high quality. The straps and handles are rugged yet padded and very comfortable.At first I thought this bag wasn't that big inside, because when all the pockets are empty, it actually compresses down into a fairly compact size. Then I realized how much capacity there is. And the compartments are so smartly designed! To give you an idea: Right now the back compartment has my iPad and 15-inch MacBook (which is sitting on a built-in cushioned bottom so that it doesn't hit the ground when I put the bag down), the middle compartment has clothing and a pair of sneakers, the outside zipper is holding my AC adapters and wires, the hard protective case on the outside top has my sunglasses and camera, and the external pocket in the middle of the bag is holding the newspaper. (And I'm not even using all the compartments; there is still room in the bottom compartment, and there are tons of zippered crevices on the insides to organize anything you've got.)The sign of a really great product is when the designers put in features I didn't even realize I needed, UNTIL I used them. I am talking specifically about the "Shove-it Pocket." This is a pocket in the middle of the bag that doesn't have a zipper, and it is accessible from the top of the bag -- you can quickly stuff things in there and pull them out quickly as needed. When I first saw this pocket I thought, "Um, this is kind of weird. I don't think I'm going to use this when I could put my stuff inside the backpack." Then I realized that the external pocket is perfect for putting in my newspaper. And my umbrella. And my water bottle. And my banana! It is expandable with adjusting straps, and everything stays put. It's a genius feature, and because it is instantly accessible, I find I use it the most out of all the compartments.The only negative I could say about this bag is that it's kind of tall. But I'm 6'1" and it fits my frame perfectly - and the height helps it hold so much!In comparison to this Thule backpack, every other backpack I've used seems cheap and poorly thought out. This bag is comfortable, functional, durable, and brilliantly thought out. I cannot recommend it strongly enough.

reviewText: This cleaner is definitely not as described. There are no "five preset cleaning cycles". It is either on or off, and will only run for three minutes before having to be reset manually. There is an on button, an off button, and a reset button that appears to do absolutely nothing.  The unit feels very flimsy and cheaply made. I am not expecting it to last very long.  It is also significantly less powerful than the unit I am replacing.  My previous unit generated 60 MHz, while this one only generates 42.  I didn't know how much of a difference this would really make, but when I put my finger in the water while the unit was running, I felt a very strong prickling sensation with the old unit. It's probably not worth the expense to ship this back for a refund, so I will just keep it till it breaks, and then get a different brand next time.  It is not even the same model number as this sale page indicates.  And the owners manual that comes with this thing is ridiculous! It reads like someone used Google Translate to convert it from Chinese into English.  Thoroughly disappointed!

description: TRG the One dye kits are EASY and FUN to use! Here are some application tips from the pros at TRG! First it is essential to thoroughly clean the item to be dyed and remove existing finishes prior to application. The type of cleaning required is different depending on the material of the item. For leather, apply the TRG Preparer (supplied in kit) and use with a (new) standard kitchen green scouring pad in order to remove dirt, shoe creams and protectors on the leather which would prevent the correct application of the dye. For synthetic leather, rub with a soft cloth soaked with TRG Preparer (supplied in kit) and dye immediately after this. (Do not use a green scourer like you do for real leather items). For canvas, wash with water and soap, apply one or two coats of dye on the damp canvas by following the below procedure Then stir the bottom of the bottle of dye (supplied in kit) with the brush (supplied in kit) until you have thoroughly mixed the dye. With the half-wrung brush, paint the joints between the sole and the leather, on sewing and scratches, ornaments, etc.. Apply one or two brushstrokes of dye on one end of the sponge (supplied in kit). Rub gently in a circular motion on the surface to be dyed, applying another brushstroke if necessary. Without adding more dye some touches can be applied with the sponge on the dyed surface in order to even up the colour. Once the first coat is dry apply a second coat by repeating the operation in order to even out the colour. Apply a third coat if needed. Once the procedure is finished, wash the sponge and the paintbrush with water in order to prevent them from drying out. It will be observed that having applied 2 or 3 coats, the quantity of dye used is very small and therefore a result of dyeing and not being painted. The leather gets smooth and flexible and the dye will never peel off. After 5 hours the dye will be completely dry and resistant to a dry or wet rub.

title: Vertx EDC Gamut Bag
description: The EDC Gamut delivers top-of-the-line features in a compact design. It contains multiple internal organizational pockets and zippered, side compartmental pockets on each side of bag. Built to carry a full load and then some, this feature-rich bag includes all the necessary elements found in a standard everyday carry pack plus game changing innovative functionality for the prepared professional.
reviewText: I was looking for a new backpack I could take to work and on business trips and this seemed to fit the bill nicely. Please know this review is through that "work" lens primarily and others may seek to use this bag for other purposes. It offers a lot of versatility as a weekend get away pack, or even a 24 hour emergency bag that's pre-packed. The bag is well-constructed and made from really durable material. There's a lot of attention to detail in both design and construction. For the reasons stated below, I'd take off a half stars as a work bag, but if someone is seeking a 48 hour "bug out bag" I'm hard pressed to think of anything better.There are a million pockets on this thing and I seem to run across a new one every time I open the bag. The zippers open from the top to the bottom of the bag which proves quite handy, When the bag is fully opened the storage areas become completely exposed which makes it very easy to access what you need. You can also engage the snap "limiters" so when traveling you can just open the very top and not expose other items within.For office/airport use, some of the pockets are not very practical. On the side pockets, there are flaps of material that make little tunnels that can hold smaller objects. I have nothing that fits there. There's also a wide-but-short zippered pocket. The zip pocket is not a very practical size and shape for work purposes, unless you use the entire outer pocket to hold glasses in a case or loose items.Even though I have not served in the military, I love MOLLE gear because it's so practical and modular. I especially like the way the outside panel of this bag covers the MOLLE section so this bag doesn't look military, but can behave that way. On the outside it looks just like a normal work backpack, unless you stow away that outer cover. I've added a few MOLLE-attached bags there and it's stellar to have them available for use. On the inside of the main compartment there are several mesh compartments that make it easy to see what is stored there.There's also a nicely padded area for a laptop and plenty of storage space for whatever you might need. Inside surface has in many places the "soft" side of velcro so you can attach things there as you wish.  For the preppers out there, there's a bendable plastic plate helping give the bag some rigidity. It can be removed and replaced with a ballistic panel. That's extreme for my use, but hey, it's a good idea to allow for that versatility. Alternately, it can hold a camelback-like water bladder. I took out the panel because it stretches the bag to full size and I'd prefer a more flexible bag to stuff under airplane seatsIn the inside of the main pocket, where there's not pockets, there is the "soft side" of Velcro everywhere. it would be really easy to stick there whatever other pockets, patches, badges, and so on, that you might need.I love how the shoulder straps are well padded. and there's also a sternum strap and waist belt. When running with a full bag though the airport with a tight flight connection, it stays in place well. If you use the back for a hiking trip or something (and it would work well for that too) you will want the extra straps.There's a pass-though panel on the back of the bad so you can slide it over the extended handle of rollaboard luggage, or even shove your arm though it if you need a shield and chose the ballistic panel. The former feature is great for travel. Hopefully the latter is never needed :-)Downsides? Time will tell, but the zippers on the most commonly used areas are not as robust as I'd like to see. They do seem durable but they tend to catch a bit when opening and closing. The zipper on the back panel is extra big and super-easy to open and shut. I think that should be the zipper gauge used on the rest of the bag.I'm 5'8" and the bag is a bit long for me. Even without the rigid back panel it will be hard to get the whole thing easily under and airplane seat. I'd prefer to see it about 4" shorter.  Vertx makes a computer bag, but it only has one strap and I need two. So I guess I'm in an awkward inbetween size.Summing up, the construction and versatility are great and it will serve quite well as a work pack -- plus other uses too. For a work backpack it's a solid four stars due to the limitations above. But for other uses the user might find it a five star item. I'm very pleased with it, would recommend it, and expect it to last through many years.

description: Fixgear Athletic Apparel latest Elite range of performance compression tight Garments.
reviewText: I ordered 3 of these initially liked them and ordered 3 more. One of the second order was this white one with multi colored arms. I had gotten the bleck version with multi colored arms in my first order and liked it enough to grab the white one the second time around.Ordering: Seller is based in South Korea.  First order arrived in 9 business days (12 days overall) and the second in 11 business days (15 overall). Both times I was notified that it has shipped, but Amazon's tracking link didn't work until the day it arrived at my post office. It is sent registered mail, meaning someone must sign for it. Your postman will attempt delivery if you are home, otherwise they leave a form and you can go down to the post office the next day and sign for it. Both times the three shirts came in one of those thick pastic clothes mailers rather than a box. No issues with damage or anything. The shirts come in their own packaging as well so they are pretty well protected.Shirts: They are labeled 100% polyester. Labeled made in Korea. The designs are dyed into the material. Nike and Under Armour have done a little of this in the past but not to the degree in these shirts. Although labeled 100% poly, they feel like part of that is elastane or some other stretchy synthetic. I read some reviews on these that said they are not compression shirts. The 6 I have received all were. They form fit to the body and do so because of the stretchy material. They are a lightweight compression shirt similar to Under Armour heat gear. Some Nike pro combat stuff is a bit thicker as are some of the winter compression items which use a small fleece layer on the inside. These fixgear shirts are well stiched and seem to be the same quality as most off the shelf compresion shirts from other brands.Sizing and fit: I am 6'3" and 205lbs with an athletic build. I used the size chart to order and went with a XXL. The chart puts me just into the lower XXL size. In other brands of compresion wear I am similarly just on the edge of XL and XXL. I thought the fixgear XXL fit just fine. The sleeve length was a bit long so no issues there and could probably accomadate someone 6'6" or so.. Torso length was also good and I have a longer torso. Fit around the chest shoulders was perfect, but did feel more like an XL in those areas. Since it is compression gear missing a size high isn't that bad and although I will order XXL again in the future as it fits me great if you are on the fence probably err one size high.Looks: Outstanding. If you are looking at this brand it is likely due to the uncommon designs and color combinations. Under Armour has some Alter Ego stuff that looks great but is twice the cost. Otherwise nothing out there really offers these neat color and design choices. Spendy compared to solid colored compression gear but at the same time fairly unique and really looks good in person and while being worn.Overall these were just what I had hoped hence why I placed a second order. To me the fabric feels the same a heat gear and other warm weather compression stuff. This is not 2XU or similar compression gear that is much thicker and will support the body, this is to form fit, look good, and keep you cool. It is of any better quality than off the shelf store brand stuff but the designs are what you are paying for, and they are very different and unique compared to what you can find in the States.I would order again. I did go to the EMFRAA site and they have some designs there that are not available on Amazon, that are even more colorful than the ones they do have on Amazon (the main body panels on those are all graphics as well, not just the sleeves or under the arms). I like paying through Amazon so I am hoping they will bring those designs over to the site.

reviewText: My daughter loves Minecraft, and she went nuts when she saw her friend got this foam sword. I'd seen pictures of it all over the place from conventions and the like, but never saw it in person until recently. Not only is the sword way bigger than I expected, it's also surprisingly comfortable to hold! You wouldn't expect that from something where the handle is pretty much made out of squares, would you?The sword measures 24 inches from tip to base and is made of two layers of foam glued to a frame/body. The sword looks just like it should, and any fan of the game won't be disappointed by its appearance. Fortunately, the foam is firm and not super soft, ensuring that you can smack things with this for hours and still have fun. If you were hoping to have a Minecraft-related costume for Halloween this year, the sword is a must!The only downside? The glue used to hold it together. This glue is very cheap and not spread out enough to keep it from pulling apart in certain areas. It looks like a lot of other people have this problem too. It's not that big of a deal since you can easily fix it yourself, but it's annoying for something that, let's be honest, is a bit overpriced. Just check on the sword every couple of uses and fix what you need to if any splitting happens.Glue quality problem aside, the Minecraft foam sword is a fun toy for anyone to mess around with. I'd just shop around and see if you can save a few bucks though.

reviewText: I got this along with a baby chick coin purse to give to my mother as a gift. The quality of this purse is so cheap! I can see them selling this same purse for at most $20 and that's giving it a huge mark up for its novelty value. It probably only cost them like two bucks to make it. The material is thin and due to the way it's been packaged for who knows how long, the purse is lumpy. The area around the tail is folded out at an unflattering angle and one side of the face is lower than the other, along with many other lumps and bumps. The purse deflates easily and probably would only look nice if it was kept quite full. However, since the material is so thin my mother is worried that filling it too much will make it break. The plastic rod in the handles also seem like they may come loose and fall out if you're not careful. I can't believe I paid so much for this! The ends tightly grip your glasses frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.Details12 inches long (each side), with 3.2-millimeter thicknessUV-resistant, molded MIDDI ends fit medium framesTough woven climbing rope with adjustable black bead91% nylon, 6% rubber, and 2% plasticNo contact above earbowWashableMade in the USAAbout CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. It is a little big for me so I sometimes have to roll the sleeves up about an inch or two but other than that, its a great coat for a great price.

description: Soft mesh cap provides breathability throughout the year. Tag line on brim reads: "Work Till You're Injured". If you're looking to set the pace with your car buddies, this is the way to go.
reviewText: I do not own this cap, so I cannot speak to the quality. But my mother was a high school English teacher, and it is her voice ingrained in my head that prompted me to write this comment.  In "work til your injured," the "your" is used incorrectly. It should be "you're," as in the contraction for "you are": work til you are injured. As is, it is the possessive form of the word and leaves me wondering, Work til your WHAT is injured? A knuckle, I'm guessing, based on the rest of the design.  I'm actually hoping this is made in China, by non english speaking folks, as that is the only excuse for such a third grade grammatical mistake. I'd hate to think a whole American crew of workers wouldn't catch that. Ugh. Otherwise, cute cap. (Note: the photo of the hat shows the incorrect grammar. In the item description, it IS correct, so it might be worth an inquiry to the company to see what is actually on the hat, before you order.)
summary: Shoulda worked as hard in school...

title: Four-Armed Mahakala Buddha Thangka
description: The Mahakala Buddha is a wrathful deity who protects his believers. Mahakala is a symbol of the power of Akshobya, who destroys demons. He wears a crown of skulls, and has three eyes. He wears horrible instruments on his body to show that he can redeem even the most terrible of objects. He can have anywhere from two to six arms and his eyebrows are like fire, while his beard consists of various hooks framing his face. Mahakala has three eyes which symbolize the fact that he can see the past, the present, and the future. His crown is made from five skulls, and these five skulls represent our five weaknesses, anger, desire, jealousy, pride, and ignorance. This Mahakala Buddha thangka was handmade in Nepal. reviewText: This is not a four-armed Mahakala - it's a six-armed Mahakala. I suppose I should have done a better job of looking at the image before ordering this. There is a shield if you want to hide the image when not in use, and the whole thing rolls up very nicely - should you actually want to roll it up. The toggles on the ends of the bar at the bottom are made of plastic and not very well attached to the bar - handle with care.The shipping container was way too long for the item, and seems to have been damaged in transit. title: Plaza Astoria Wall/Door-Mount Jewelry Armoire, Cherry
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Jewelry Accessories', 'Jewelry Boxes & Organizers', 'Jewelry Armoires']
description: JA1448CH Features: -Jewelry armoire mirror.-Full length mirror hides a secret jewelry armoire.-Framed mirror.-Attaches to either wall or hangs on door with special brackets supplied. Construction: -Wood, metal and glass construction. Color/Finish: -Cherry finish.
reviewText: Omg, I kid you not when I tell you that I simply love this product!  Can't imagine too many of us gals who wouldn't want one of these armoires.  If you've amassed a sizeable collection of jewelry over the years and have much of it shoved into boxes and drawers (or just have it strewn all over the place!), displaying your stuff in this cleverly thought-out armoire will finally give order to the chaos (lol!)  Go to the trouble of untangling those necklaces so you can hang them...and they will remain tangle-free - hooray!  There are 24 hooks for long necklaces, but you can get about 4 on each hook.  There are 12 hooks for short necklaces a/o bracelets but, again, you can pack more on the hooks.  There are provisions for 50 pair of earrings (100 slots), but with many types of earrings (wire hook and some post), you can totally fit the pair into one slot, instead of taking up 2 slots!  It's very easy to hang your earrings: through the hole, sitting in the slot, even a combo of using the hole and the upper rim...anyway, it's all good...!Above the interior mirror (which is a great size, and quite handy!), you have 52 ring slots and 12 wider slots where you can put in things like thin bangles.  This area is foamy, so one could conceivably push in the sharp part of, say, a brooch.  You have 12 bins, and in those areas, I've put my watches, some pendants, and some larger hoop earrings I couldn't figure out how to put in the earring slots (without them jutting out...)What else can I say?  I really, really love seeing my jewelry in order!  The quality of this item is very nice - the cherry wood looks good, and matches my other wood very well.  I chose to hang it on my door (although you are provided with the option of wall-mounting it).  The thin, black, metal door brackets they provide are extremely simple to screw to the back of the case.  I hung this on a white door, and didn't like how the black brackets looked in contrast, so I spray-painted the brackets white (million times better!)  The exterior full-length mirror is very nice, not warped at all.  Also, I want to mention that I put some velcro between the back of the case and the door, as this door is open and shut often.Showed my lovely teenaged nieces this armoire a short while ago - well, it sure does take a lot to impress a teen these days, but, I tell you, they flipped for this thing...FLIPPED!  I will be more than pleased to buy this really wonderful item for each of their upcoming birthday  ;-)

reviewText: I bought this watch 5yrs ago as a way to keep up with my newborn twins nightly feedings.  (which, between the indiglo light and the multiple timers worked very well!)  I wore it 24/7, overnight, and in the shower.  The band died at about one year, and I chucked the timepiece in my nightstand.  4yrs later I started running and wanted something to keep track of my intervals.  The timepiece still worked, so I bought some industrial strength, sticky-backed velcro and a piece of elastic legband from a craft/sewing store.  I cut out a circle of velcro and stuck it to the back of the watch, stuck a matching velcro circle on the band, and then added some velcro to the ends of the wristband so that I could adjust it to fit my wrist.  It's not pretty, and I have to wear the timepiece on the inside of my wrist so that it doesn't catch on anything, but it's worked beautifully for running all year.  This week the battery has finally died (after 5yrs - not bad), so I will probably break down and buy another one.

reviewText: What kid doesn't dream of being Spiderman? And what could be cooler than having web shooting ability? The Mega Blaster Web Shooter seemed like an ideal way to get one step closer to realizing our fantasies of being a superhero icon. But what sounds like a promising concept fails almost entirely in execution.The glove apparatus, for one thing, is pretty darn flimsy and ill-fitting. You can hook a water cartridge or a can of web fluid up to the glove and release a stream via trigger. It's so awkward, though, it takes the fun out of the possibility. You should be able to run around, engage the enemy, and naturally unleash a web. As is, you've got to focus to get anything to happen and to not break the apparatus.While the water attachment is fine, who wants another water gun when you can shoot webs? What exactly is web fluid? Well, seems pretty much like wildly expensive silly string. BEFORE THINKING ABOUT THIS PURCHASE, CHECK THE REFILL COST OF THIS ITEM. You will be amazed in all the wrong ways. It's the most expensive silly string you've ever seen. There are plenty of warnings about what not to shoot the web on (pretty much anything indoors), so this limits the usefulness quite a bit as well.Great idea, but certainly not worth the investment. KGHarris, 8/12.
summary: A Great Idea, But Iffy Execution, Dampen My Superhero Dreams

description: Heads will turn as you carry this Henbag". It is sure to bring a smile to yourself and others each time you carry it. Fun gift!"
reviewText: This is great for some grins and giggles -- "Wait!  I'll get that out of my Hen Bag" -- this bag is a scream.Very durable, giant funny zipper, well-adhered red handles.  What a great gift.*** Updated -- I have been carrying the purse since I received it.  There is a slight smell of off-gassing, more noticeable to my small children who are closer to it when I am carrying the bag.The zipper is very strong.  The opening is 5" or so -- I have a rather large wallet, and it slips inside with room to spare.  The inside pouch is roomy, and because the hen is light-permeable, it is not a dark cavern in there.  You can see what you are loking for.  There is a small sewn pocket inside -- I keep a lipstick and a bunch of kleenex and hand sanitizer in it.  Good size handles, even comfortable over winter outerwear.  I added a carabiner clip to one handle to keep my keys handy at all times.I took my Hen Bag (we named her "Mrs. Tweedy" after the Farmer's wife in the "Chicken Run" movie) on a long tour of the national parks in Utah.  She went with us to Zion, Bryce, Capitol Reef, Canyonlands, and Arches.  (Posted some photos)  She was extremely practical -- all dirt and sand wiped right off her rubber feathers, and she is basically waterproof, snowproof, and slushproof.  She's the right size to hold a couple plastic water bottles and the map.  We noticed that she can express "moods" (Again, see photos) -- jaunty, unamused, resigned, affectionate.My kids got into the Hen Bag -- *really* into her.  They went a little wild on naming her -- they got way off into the weeds.  Some examples: Hen-cess Leia, Jabba the Henn, Hen Solo (like it!), Obi Hen Kenobi, Luke Egglayer (I know), Hen-peror Palpatine... you get the drift.  They were calling our car the Mill-HEN-ium Falcon.  Riotous laughter...Anyway, Mrs. Tweedy is durable and lovable.  I got a ton of favorable comments on her.  She went everywhere and stayed positive despite crowded car conditions, somewhat smelly children, and a surfeit of National Parks dirt.  She was quiet in restaurants and never complained about the long drives, or about getting the last shower.  Wonderful traveling companion.I wish she had a "clucking" noise.  She would be spectacular with sound.  Also, an egg-shaped rubber coin purse or keychain would be a good addition.

reviewText: I purchased a pair of these to use for cross training (plyometrics, strength training) and will be returning them promptly. title: Timex 50lap Sleek Mens Ironman
description: A new take on the classic Timex ironman watch. The sleek 50-lap version takes it to the next level and beyond. Key Features:.Chrono training log stores workouts by date, with best lap, average lap and the total segment time.Total run format/synchro timer maintains total activity time (less time paused during workout) and overall running time.2 interval timers settable up to 24 hours with automatic interval repetition counter.All-day white reflector display.INDIGLO night-light with NIGHT-MODE feature..Water-resistant 100m.
reviewText: Aug 20,2013 I lost the watch on an overseas trip, and promptly re-ordered the same watch when I returned.=======July 8, 2013 Editing my original review below from Nov 2012. The watch has been working just fine. I have no problem with "hair trigger" buttons. And so far the band has held up well. So - I strongly recommend this watch, particularly if you need the "weekly" alarm feature.=========================================I've had Timex digital watches for years now, because I like the styling and I need the Countdown Timer and Alarm features. This time I was particularly looking for a version that has the "Weekly" alarm feature, i.e. can be set for a specific day/time (e.g. every Wed at 11:30); this is in addition to the more standard "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends" alarm options. Many watches on the Timex website mistakenly indicate Weekly when you first look at the descriptions, but on the downloaded PDFs, they says only "Daily, Weekdays, Weekends", and not "Weekly". Some of these watches are similarly incorrectly advertised on Amazon, but I attribute the fault to Timex, not to Amazon.  I actually bought one from Amazon and immediately returned it when I realized the Weekly alarm didn't exist (no probem; thanks Amazon). The only Timex I knew about with the "weekly" feature was another Ironman model T54281. I had owned this once before, but vowed not to buy it again because the band breaks within a short period and is not replaceable; this problem is noted in the many critical reviews on both the Timex and Amazon websites. I was getting discouraged, until somehow, after more web browsing, I found the T5K335, which does have the "weekly" feature (confirmed when I downloaded the PDF from the Timex website), as well as a band that appeared reasonably durable. So I ordered it from Amazon. After a few weeks, so far so good; but still hoping about the strap - seems better than the T5K335, but maybe not as durable as some other Timex watches. The band is "integrated", i.e. it goes all around the watch and is not replaceable. Why does Timex have to chose a seemingly less durable band for its "Weekly" alarm watches. For this reason I deduct 1 star.The following sums up my experience:The right Timex I wanted to seekBut my chances were seeming quite bleakTrue, they all take a lickingAnd keep right on tickingBut few alarms chime once a week
summary: A "Weekly" alarm, with a decent band

reviewText: I am just getting my feet wet into the sport of cycling, so everything that I am getting is entry level quality and thus I have nothing else to compare these shoes to, I have never wore other brand or more expensive cycling shoes.The quick review is that these are the biggest bargain you are going to find out there, order your pair before they run out, remember it is May, the beginning of cycling season, so everybody is buying their gear.Now, the more detailed review:These run a little small in size depending if you have a wide fat foot or long skinny feet. I usually ware 10.5 or 11 USA size depending on the brand of shoes, but I had to order these size 44 which is the equivalent of a 9.5-10 USA size. So, if you have a fat foot or have bunions then order the size 45, but if you have skinny feeds, get the size 44.Comfort. I find these shoes very comfortable for their purpose, as long as you on the bike, you don't feel them, the size 44 fits me very snug and it works well for when I am pulling up on the pedals, I feel my feet, the shoes and the pedals as one piece. Note, because of the big size cleat on the bottom, these shoes are not meant to be walking a lot, and you better be careful on tile floors because you will slip due to the plastic cleats.Quality. These look great, they are not leather, but they look very nice. The craftsmanship is perfect, I don't see anything wrong that could give me a sign of any trouble, except the they only had them in white and they will get dirty soon. But, then again I am gentile with my equipment. I am sure there are people out there that even if you give them steel shoes they will find a way to ware them out and destroy them. But if you careful with your equipment, these look like they can last a very long time.Features.Part of the shoes are mesh opening to keep your feet cool but you can hardly tell. The two bottom laces are velcro, but the top lace has a plastic belt with a nice ratchet mechanism that works really well, and again, as long as you treat it with respect, I don't foresee any trouble there. These use the LOOK system, the cleats attach very well to the shoes and hold very secure to the pedals. Although, the LOOK style has bigger size cleats, it still is a pain to click into the pedals, so shoes with cleats are not meat for high traffic city riding, for that just get regular pedals to be safe.Conclusion.This is the best deal out there for the new comer. Excellent quality for being entry level. I love the LOOK system. The kit includes the shoes, the cleats and the pedals, everything that you need to start riding. These are more expensive then mountain bike version, but are very well worth the extra $20 not only in terms of the LOOK system which is better, but also in terms of the overall quality of the product as a whole.Last but not least, let me school those who like me, have no clue about the difference between a mountain bike vs road bike shoes difference.The cleats, the piece that attaches to the bottom of the shoes is much smaller for the mountain bike type of shoes, and I find two drawback about this style of shoes, first I find it much harder to click into the pedal because one has to be more accurately since the cleat is so small. Second, because the cleats are so small, it doesn't cover a big portion of the shoe sole, and you can feel that when you pulling up on the pedal.On the other hand, the road bike style shoes which these are, use the type "LOOK" system, this style has a much bigger cleat piece that is much easier to click into the pedal and because it is a big cleat, it attaches to a bigger surface of the shoes sole, so when you are pedaling up, the whole shoes come up, it doesn't feel as if you are going to yank the shoe from the petal. In short, the conclusion is for you to go for the LOOK type of shoes, not the mountain bike type.
summary: Amazing product for an amazing price.

reviewText: Sometime during the Fall of 2013, I decided to set my furnace thermostat at 65F and just leave it there until turning it off in the Spring of 2014. San Diego doesn't get very cold during the winter so the furnace would seldom be running. It's not much of a sacrifice to comfort. In fact, it's rather nice to have cool air around you and something that hasn't been dried out by a furnace. Now and then it gets bit chilly and for those times I had a couple light-weigt  fleece jackets.I went close to a month into this winter heating plan when my mother-in-law gave me a Mountain Hard Wear Ghost Whisperer Down Jacket (Silver Color) for a Christmas present. Nice. It was ultra light-weight and weighed barely more than a normal long-sleeved shirt. It was warm and comfortable without being hot or feeling like a heavy jacket. It felt good inside or outside the house. Zip it up and it resisted mild winds quite well. I could put it on as a liner under a heavier jacket for added warmth during real cold episodes. For traveling, the entire jacket was so small and light that it would fold up and fit in one of it's own pockets. Easy to care for. This is a real "cool" jacket. I love it!Gary Peterson
summary: Ultra-Light, Good Fit and Feel, Warm but not Too Warm, Good Inside or Outside. I love It!

description: Open mesh knitting on the top of foot. Reinforced heel and toe. Elastic support around the arch.
reviewText: I am a serious runner (1200 miles per year) and am always interested in trying new socks for running. I previously bought the cushioned version of these socks (which I have reviewed on Amazon and really like), and wanted to try the non-cushioned mesh version, which is a thinner pair of socks. After running in them, it is clear why they have earned mainly five star reviews.First a word about sizing. If in doubt, order a size up. I wear a size 8 street shoe and 9 1/2 running shoe. When I first ordered the cushioned version I got a medium size, which fit me--but just barely. So I ordered this sock in a large and it fits much better.This sock is very comfortable to wear and lets my feet breath while running. Unlike cheaper socks, these socks are not drenched with sweat after a long run (10 miles).I use minimalist running shoes that are not cushioned (Nike Free Run+). However, even with the heavily cushioned running shoes that I used to wear before I read Born to Run, these socks still fit comfortably (NOTE: if you use heavily cushioned running shoes, then the cushioned version of these socks will probably be too snug a fit since they are thicker).I also own the wool version of these socks, which fit and perform just as well as these socks. In cold weather both the wool and cool max socks keep my feet equally warm. However, wool does have the advantage of staying warm when wet, which I have put to the test when accidentally stepping into slush puddles when running outside in the winter.Bottom line: These socks are not inexpensive, but work really well. I recommend them for runners.

title: Under Armour UA Hustle Storm MD Duffle Bag
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Luggage & Travel Gear', 'Gym Bags', 'Sports Duffels']
description: UA Storm gear uses a DWR finish to repel water without sacrificing breathability. Adjustable, padded shoulder strap with HeatGear® for total comfort. 2 large vented end pockets, 1 expandable for laundry and shoes. Dimensions: 23" x 12" x 11". reviewText: My brother's gotten interested in fighting recently after I let him practice punches on some of my pads. Right now he's using a little drawstring backpack to hold his gloves, but he's going to need something bigger and better when he gets more gear like shin guards, headgear, bag gloves, etc. I ordered him this Hustle Storm duffle bag in what's gotta be the coolest color ever- hyper green. I have theUnder Armour PTH Victory Medium Team Duffel Bagfor my gear and absolutely love it. After this one arrived in the mail, I kind of regret not getting him the same bag as me but in a different color. The Hustle Storm duffel bag isn't terrible, but it's not great either. Truth be told, I'd probably give it 4 stars if I didn't have a much better one myself to compare it to. It's just that compared to it, this one is a bit of a letdown. Let's start with the good though.The main storage compartment is huge. I took out the gear from my bag and put it in this one, and everything fit just fine. I was able to store an Everlast Thai pad, two pairs of gloves, two Mantis mitts and shorts, and there was still plenty of room for more. The zippers on each compartment open easily and close perfectly. I really liked the little UA logo zipper pull thingy on the Storm pocket too. The side compartment that zips has a vented area, making this ideal for your dirty clothes or shoes. I wear a size 11 in Nike shoes, and was able to put a pair in this compartment without any problems. Then there's the two handles that can be held together with a little velcro closure for easy carrying. Finally, the hyper green color is just plain incredible and I wish my Victory bag had that option! Trust me when I say that it looks -much- better in person than it does in the stock image, where it looks more like a lime green. If you want something that's going to be easy to see wherever you go, hyper green is what you want.That's a lot of good, right? Unfortunately, the quality of the bag itself isn't one of the things mentioned above. This bag is very thin. So thin that I said "...oh" out loud when I took it out of the packaging. Sure enough, it's nowhere near as thick as my Victory bag. Maybe it's because this one was made to repel 'the elements', but that's only going to really help you if you use this for camping or hiking. And if you need a bag for either of those, there are better options out there. Why get a thin bag that can be punctured easily? I don't trust this material for anything more than gym use. Even the shoulder strap feels wimpy. As for the Storm pocket, all you're going to use this thing for is your phone, mp3 player, keys and maybe your wallet. It's too small to be used for much else. There's another pocket on the side of the bag you could use for a towel or something. It's just a 2/3-pocket that's open and doesn't close in any way. There are no interior pockets either.For the same price as the Victory bag, you're getting one made with a thinner material and with less storage. Let me say that one more time- FOR THE SAME PRICE. That being said, I strongly recommend the Victory over this one unless you only need something for the gym. Yes, the Hustle Storm duffel bag is lighter, but I wouldn't be surprised if the plastic hooks that the shoulder strap fastens to the bag with broke if you put too much stuff in it. Here you get a ton of cool color options, so determine if you need style over strength. If any stores in your area carry this bag, go check it out before ordering.

title: Ape Case Compact Backpack for Digital SLR Cameras ACPRO1810W
description: The ACPRO1810W DSLR Compact Backpack is the perfect backpack when you want to carry a decent amount of equipment, but don't want a huge and cumbersome case. Compact and light, yet surprisingly high capacity, the ACPRO1810W is designed with multiple compartments that can be reconfigured to hold different lenses, cameras and accessories. You can carry a digital SLR cameras with attached lens, with additional room for 2-3 more lenses and a flash. With Ape Case’s clean, discreet design, You can safely transport your valuable cargo without calling attention to what's inside. Padded and water resistant, all Ape Case Backpacks feature our signature Hi-Vis Yellow interior, and built-in retractable water proof any-weather cover. Hi-Vis Yellow makes seeing and finding your equipment and accessories inside your Ape Case much easier than in other brand’s standard black or grey interiors and our weather cover offers any-weather protection, a feature usually found in high priced gear or available as an accessory. All zippers feature high styled zipper pulls and accents and are covered with weather resistant flaps. The large front zippered pocket is large enough to house an iPad and can be accessed without opening the main camera compartment and has plenty of pockets and compartments to hold accessories like filters, batteries and other items like pens and paper etc. There is a convenient key fob in the front compartment with a spring-loaded clasp for your keys or other valuable. At the top of the case is a slick MP3 player pocket with a portal for the head phone cord so you can house your music player and listen to music while wearing the backpack. There is a large outside pocket on both sides of the backpack suitable for carrying a water bottle or other accessories. Exterior dimensions (WxDxH) 10x9x13 Interior dimensions 9x4.25x12; Limited Lifetime warranty
reviewText: I settled on this backpack style camera case for my Canon D40 and accessories.  I got the bag yesterday and my camera fit in nicely.  The additional compartments seemed adequate for any additional lenses,etc., however; I would have liked more space for personal items in the front and side pockets but keep in mind that this is a "compact" case.  Overall, it was attractive and the perfect size for me... not too big and bulky, and not too small, plus I liked the yellow interior.  I also liked the extra security in the straps with clips on each side of the pack that secured the front flap to the sides.  For me, it was an important safety feature in case of zipper failure. Though having the camera compartment located at the top of the bag seems like a more protected location than at the bottom of the bag, it made the bag top heavy and prone to falling over.Anyway, I purchased this bag from "Amazon Warehouse Deals" for less than the "new" price.  Amazon labeled the bag as used but in "like new" condition.  I believe it was a bag that had been returned and was, in fact, unused.  I was very pleased with the appearance, which looked brand spanking new inside and out.  But, when I attempted to zip it closed, it didn't close.  The zipper was defective and though it moved freely, the zipper kept opening up.  This was my first experience with Amazon Marketplace and it probably will be my last.  Like New items are supposed to be in like new condition and should have been thoroughly checked out by Amazon before re-selling it.  Though the return postage was paid by Amazon, I had to re-package the bag, print out a packing slip and shipping label, then take it to the UPS store to return it, which was a bit of a hassle.  I now have to wait an undetermined amount of time before I get my refund and that's a drawback too.The bottom line is that this seemed like a nice bag but for the money you can find a better deal.  I ended up ordering the Canon 200EG Deluxe Digital SLR Camera Backpack Case for $39.95.  It is new and made by Canon so I figured I couldn't go wrong there.  Since there are already 1,600+ reviews, with an average of 4 1/2 stars, I probably won't bother to write a review... unless the zipper is busted!

title: Toynami Futurama Bender Knitted Hat
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Novelty', 'Clothing', 'Men', 'Accessories', 'Hats & Caps', 'Bomber Hats']
description: Ever wanted to wear your favorite Futurama characters with you wherever you go? Well now you can with Futurama knit hats. These knit hats feature Bender and Nibblers faces with knitted details. Perfect for cold weather or just showing off your love for Futurama.
reviewText: I got the Bender knitted hat first, then the Nibbler one.  This Bender one isn't quite as well "sculpted" as the Nibbler version.  All you get is the antenna and the eyes, where as Nibbler you get the whole face, so it's harder for your average person to see what it is, especially if they aren't familiar with Futurama.Me, myself and I, being a good fan of the show, just couldn't resist getting these knitted hats.  I work in a warehouse environment that has no air conditioning to speak of early in the mornings and it can get pretty cold during the winter time, so why not?  Anyone who has ever seen Futurama should recognize the theme of this hat, but people who are not may see something else.  I know a few other reviewers have commented on the particular nature of how the features of this hat look and the comments people have given them...well it's true, so be prepared to receive them.  The picture for the item is pretty accurate so you can see that the antenna on top does look rather "bulbous"...almost "falice"?  I've gotten a number of "dick" or even "booby"-head comments/jokes from the guys where I work (since most of them have no idea what "Futurama" is, let alone who "Bender" is!).  I tell people I won't judge them for what's on their mind when they give me those comments, but honestly it does kind of look like that.  If it was shaped better (a thinner shaft, a smaller/rounder top), then it would look more like Bender's antenna than a grey piece of human anatomy.The hat is pretty soft and comfortable.  The outside is knitted of course and the inside is a fleece material.  There are tags in the back of the head that you may want to cut off because you can feel these sometimes, scratching the back of your head, when you put it on.  This hat will stretch a bit, so it can fit a number of different size heads, but when I put it on it does stretch a bit to fit me and I don't have a big head, nor a lot of hair, so if you have what can be categorized as a big head or have lots of hair, it may not fit you.One thing that I'm knocking off a star for is what I already mentioned up top, for the slightly misshapen features.  Another one is that it doesn't have any strings or straps or anything to allow you to tie down the ear flaps under your chin to help keep your ears warm.  The ear flaps just hang loose and can keep your ears semi-warm, but if you're in the wind or one good cold breeze and they don't make a bit of difference.
summary: It's Alright, But Unless They Know Futurama, People Won't Get It!

title: Optic Nerve Axel Polarized Sunglass
description: When you put yourself in extreme conditions, simply reducing glare is not enough. Enter the Optic Nerve Axel polarized sunglasses, which add such benefits as lightweight comfort and long-lasting durability to the mix. The sunglasses owe their superior fit to Optic Nerve's 4-Point Frame Fit technology, which helps the glasses stay snug well over the life of the glass. Optic Nerve's engineers put the glasses through a meticulous specification process, measuring tip-to-tip distance, pin-to-pin distance, mid-temple distance, and panascopic angle. The process ensures that each frame is well balanced and offers a secure, comfortable feel right off the display. Wearers will also love the line-less spring temple hinge, which further improves the fit to enhance comfort and security. And the glasses are guaranteed to last thanks to the nickel silver alloy construction. The alloy--which is used for all frames and components--is not only durable and resilient, but is also coated for hypoallergenic performance.Optic Nerve Lens TechnologiesPolarized lenses have an invisible horizontal filter integrated into the lens. This filter is designed to eliminate reflected (or polarized) light, more commonly referred to as glare. When sunlight is reflected off a surface, it becomes concentrated and even more intense. Polarized lenses filter out 99.9 percent of this reflected glare, helping the glasses perform in bright sun and variable light conditions. The lenses also undergo a process called Focalpoint Lens Technology, which eliminates prismatic distortion by shifting the optical sweet spot from its natural position and placing it directly in front of the eye. This produces clear optical clarity throughout the entire peripheral range. And all Optic Nerve lenses (including clear) meet or exceed the U.S. government and FDA standards for impact-resistance and UV protection.About Optic NerveOptic Nerve has been a leader in the sport sunglass industry for nearly 25 years. The company has worked hard to create a dynamic manufacturing process that stands for intelligence, awareness, and style: intelligence in the construction process, using only the finest frame material and highest-quality lenses; awareness in the company's operations and the nonprofit youth organizations it works with; and style that speaks for itself in the Optic Nerve product line. The employees at Optic Nerve have spent countless years in the mountains of Colorado testing sunglasses, helping produce the finest sunglasses on the market.

description: The Timex 10 Lap Ironman provides entry-level functionality with the quality, tradition, and durability of the Ironman brand. The watch has Stopwatch, Timer, and Alarm for all of your timing needs.Alarm settable for Daily, Weekday, Weekend, or Weekly with 5min backup.Indiglo night-light.100m water resistant.
reviewText: I've had it for two days and compared it to my Casio Men's DW5600E G-Shock repeatedly. I just like this one better and I'm shocked - no pun intended. Durability is the biggest question in my mind - so time will tell - but at least I can read the numbers on this easily and user interface is awesome - better than expected on a watch at this price.Here's what I really love about this watch:- 50% lighter than the g-shock- Sightly thinner - it's close though- I can actually read the numbers - my eyes aren't what they used to be and the Timex numbers are a good 50% larger than my g-shock.- Fantastic contrast of numbers against background: much better than my g-shocks - the background is whiter - so easier to read.- Smoother, sleeker design and a few mm thinner makes all the difference with my dress shirts - I think it's the sleekness more than just being thinner. It doesn't 'catch' on my shirt sleeves - which I find very annoying about my two g-shocks unfortunately.Additional Pros- Buttons are easier to work with than the G-shock. (could be a con though - we'll see)- User interface feels more modern and intuitive.- Dual time zone and easy, intuitive switching is really nice- Band is thinner and seems a better fit for my thinner wrists- Band lock: I was annoyed at first like some else said. But, now I really like it. It locks in the band strap nicely so there's no movement at all. If you're someone who removes your watch a lot, you may be annoyed. If you don't, you'll probably love this.- Indiglo 8-hour night mode is pretty cool - jury is still out on this one - but I think I like it.- Very inexpensive - disposable in fact.Cons- Buttons are easy to press. It's more of a 'pro' for me right now but I just bought this a few days ago and can see how it may become a 'con' like some other reviewers mentioned. Time will tell and I will definitely edit my review if this becomes an issue. At the moment I like how much easier they are to deal with compared to my G-shocks.- Durability: potential con - I couldn't find any reviews addressing how long these last. This feels less substantial than your average g-shock watch. But, they're super cheap so even a couple of years would be nice. But, the g-shocks last forever and even if you beat on them, they still look great. This one - I don't know - I hope it proves to be indestructible like the g-shocks but it doesn't feel as industrial strength. Time will tell. It's so light, maybe it just feels less rugged comparatively but it will be just as good.It's a keeper for now - but if the watch face (acrylic?) ends up being anywhere near as rugged as the G-shocks - I'll be a very happy camper.

description: Croakies Suiters are lightweight and remarkably soft to the touch -- you may occasionally forget you're wearing them. The ends tightly grip all small to medium sized frames, so while you may lose yourself in your favorite activity, your glasses will remain securely strapped to your head.Details14-inch length (each side) and 0.5-inch widthKnitted cotton yarnAdjustable slider beadColorfast, washable, air dry, no bleachMade in the USAAbout CroakiesIn 1977, a local ski patrolman from Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in Wyoming came up with an idea for an eyewear retainer that would grip his shades through all kinds of alpine adventures. Using an old wetsuit and some sharp scissors, he made the first pair of eyewear retainers. The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. Croakies products are sold by retailers throughout the United States and in over 30 countries around the world. description: Terry Bath Robe Robe is crafted from soft, durable 100% Egyptian Cotton. Quite simply, Egyptian cotton produces longer fibers (up to twice as long as a standard cotton fiber). reviewText: What a great robe! I ordered it in Sage and was surprised with how quickly it shipped and arrived. The packaging was great. It arrived in a thick plastic bag with a ribbon tied around the robe, and included a personal note and information about the robe. This is especially nice if you are planning on sending it to someone as a gift: you can rest assured knowing it comes nicely packaged.The first thing I noticed about the robe when I unwrapped it and picked it up was how thick and heavy it is. This is one robe that will definitely keep you warm in the cold winter months. The color is beautiful and looks even better than it does in the picture. At first the robe did not feel as soft as I was hoping it would, and tons of little fabric balls fell off when I lifted it up. Since I wash everything I get before using it anyway, I headed straight to the laundry room. Following the directions, I washed it and put it in the dryer. As I expected, the lint screen was covered, but this was good as it got rid of all the extra fabric balls. There was no color fading either, and the robe is now much softer!I am 5'3" and this robe fits perfectly. I want to mention here that I really appreciate the measurements being supplied as part of the robe's description as it makes finding the correct size a cinch! The robe falls just above my ankles, and wraps all the way around me without it gaping open below the knees. You know how some robes just barely come together in the front so when you tie them closed they still gape open letting in cold air? Well this robe is made so that it has enough fabric to overlap once closed, so it won't gape open when moving around. It also comes with a nice long belt, and two deep pockets which are very handy!Another thing I like about this robe is that the material is very absorbent. If you are still damp after your shower, this robe will quickly absorb the water leaving you completely dry. It is quite thick which adds a bit of weight to it, and keeps you nice and warm without being too heavy.Since I first washed the robe, there has not been any more fabric balls/lint coming off of it to drop on the floor or stick to your skin. I have washed it one more time, and it keeps getting softer with each wash. There was still some lint on the dryer screen, but nowhere near the amount there was the first time I washed it! Looking at the stitching, you can see -and feel- that this robe is very well-made and should last a long time!Taken all together, these features combine to make a very comfortable and luxurious robe at an amazingly affordable price! I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a new robe either for themselves, their family or a friend; and with the Holidays coming soon, this robe would make a wonderful gift!

The ingenious device was based on the design of a Chinese finger trap, and quickly became a hit with local ski patrolers. Demand picked up quickly for the patrolman's invention, which was initially nameless. Back in the seventies, the Jackson Hole ski patrol used the nickname "croakies" when they couldn't think of a word (think "thing- amajig"), but it finally stuck on the world'd first neoprene eyewear retainer.Croakies headquarters are still in Jackson Hole, with production in Bozeman, Montana. The inspiration remains the same -- to create eyewear retainers and accessories that provide comfort, style, durability, and functionality to active people of all ages. reviewText: I purchased a few of these padlocks to have on hand for luggage and similar items when traveling. They are adequate, but don't count on these for anything other than low-level security of your belongings. The lock uses a thin cable rather than solid metal, and could be easily cut with a decent pair of wire cutters. Just know that up front and be okay with it. It will keep honest people honest, and keep little fingers away from things - but it won't stop a real thief.I had some trouble following the simple directions for setting the combination. It works as described, but it took more than one try and took me quite a few "open" and "lock" repetitions before I started to feel comfortable that it works. A few times, my new combo would not open the lock - and then next time it would.It provides you with only a 3 digit combination, so the security is not strong. Try not to use an easy to guess number! The number dials do not index really well, and it is not always easy to dial-in your combination. You can be off by a fraction of a turn and not realize it.At the price, and for limited purpose, this is a decent lock. For anything I care about securing though - I will want something better.

reviewText: The Bracelet T-Bars are exactly what I expected & wanted, & were received in great condition, despite the way in which they were delivered. I received my purchases in 3 boxes, because of the number & sizes of items I ordered. The 2 largest boxes were all dented in; it was obvious they had been thrown around quite a bit. Also, there was only one strip of tape across the tops of each box, & both of the boxes were opened where the tape had detached. My concerns were that some items would be missing, or that they would be damaged. However, to my relief, everything was in good order. For future deliveries, I recommend that the distributor either put two strips of tape across the tops of each box, or invest in a better grade of tape that will not come off! This won't stop me from making future orders, but it would be cheaper for companies to tape the boxes better, rather than to possibly have to replace items that fall out of the boxes.I have lots of bracelets, anklets & necklaces, but had run out of space for my costume jewelry; it was all over the tops of my bedroom furniture! I keep my good jewelry in a nice jewelry box, & decided it was time to separate them & was unable to find what I wanted in stores in Baton Rouge, LA. Of course I should have saved myself from wasting time & gas, & checked with Amazon on-line when I first got the idea to look for these jewelry displays!! I've made many purchases from y'all in the past, finding furniture & other things,for reasonable costs & free delivery to my door!!I purchased a couple of the jewelry displays for myself, & have reorganized all of my jewelry; my bedroom dresser tops now look so much better, & it's so much easier to find what I'm looking for!! i bought the others for birthday & Christmas gifts. I already have sets of bangle bracelets & necklaces for the T-Bars, & am sure my daughters-in-law, granddaughters, etc, will appreciate & use the items for years to come! I'm so glad that I found Amazon a few years ago! I am disabled, & your company really makes my life a lot easier!

reviewText: So I have a ton of bags for computers.  My current computer is smaller than the 16" that this was built for, but I thought it would be just fine so I went ahead and ordered it.  There are some great features in this bag, but the one that isn't so great is due to the computer size I have, so that probably can't be the fault of the bag.Here's what the deal is: inside the second compartment, the area for the laptop, there is an inner pocket where you slide the computer in, then a piece of velcro elasic that holds it into place.  The velcro is about 2" wide and has a lot of stretch to it.  That's the part that I am having a problem with.  My computer is a couple inches smaller, so when I go to cinch it in tight, the velcro strap is too big.  If somehow the place to attach the velcro TO was a bit longer then I think this issue would be solved immediately.Lots of great pockets in this bag, two water bottle spots, but by far my favorite feature can be found on the bottom of the bag.  A zippered "pouch"....or so it seems....open it up, and you'll find one of the coolest features of this bag - rain gear for your bag!  Honest to goodness, the backpack comes with its own rain fly that has elastic and fits nice and snug over your bag.  A feature I have never seen before and one that I thought made this bag stand out quite a bit over my other bags.The bag is comfortable to wear, sits high on your back, and has lots of adjustments. With laptops so light these days, this bag is not too bulky and seems to fit just right.  Would recommend to anyone who needs to travel with their 16" laptop.

reviewText: This stuff rocks (or rather, it rock-ets? Call the pun police). When the weather turns cold and I switch back to close-toed shoes, I always lament how smelly they get during the course of the day. I was about ready to suck up the cramped-ness that comes with odor-eater foot pads, but this Rocket Pure spray had such good reviews that I figured it was worth a shot. And I'm glad I did, because this stuff is great -- I've now used it on leather boots, synthetic-fabric flats, and sneakers, and just a couple sprays in each shoe stamps out unpleasant odor. I will say, the smell is VERY menthol-heavy at first, which was initially off-putting, but it mellows out into a fresh peppermint scent after a bit -- and now my closet smells like an Altoids tin whenever I open it (and that's a positive thing!). title: Patagonia R1 Pull Over Fleece Jacket - Men's
description: Patagonia Men's R1 Pullover
reviewText: The 2013 redesign of the R1 Pullover made it the best midlayer fleece for active use today. It goes well beyond everything else currently available in both form and function.Patagonia shifted from a single fabric design to a zonal, dual fabric construction. The main body of the pullover uses a fleece that is very light weight and compressible yet warm, while areas that often get damp (underarms, underarm gussets, collar, cuffs) use an even lighter and faster drying fleece. Both fabrics have a smooth, shiny finish to make layering over the garment easier.The key to the high performance of the fleece fabrics is how they are made. Small squares of fleece are woven in a grid pattern on the inner face of a stretchy, translucent backing. This gives the fabrics the ability to be both warm and breathable. The fleece squares hold warm air while the thin backing allows moisture and vapor to pass between each square, unimpeded. Much better than earlier generation fleece!Other details which set the R1 apart are thumbholes on the sleeves, cuffs that stay put when pushed up, an extra long main zipper that makes it easy to dump lots of heat quickly, and a chest pocket that doubles as a second heat vent.My only caveats are that the cut and fit are fairly slim since the R1 needs to fit under a shell or other outer layer and, yes, it costs a lot more than those boxy, heavy el-cheapo fleeces that are a common sight at discount and fast-fashion stores. But if you want your fleece to be more than just a glorified baby's blanket, the R1 Pullover is well worth its price. And let's face it, if you don't lead a reasonably active lifestyle, you don't need this kind of technical garment.Five stars.
