reviewText: I am very disappointed in this watch, the F-91W.I have owned a different watch, the Casio W-71 for many years, and find it to be a versatile watch, but the band just broke (as they do after several years). I purchased the F-91W awhile back as a future replacement, but found it lacking seriously when I had to use it. I would have sent it back, but considering the cost of shipping, it was not worth it.The features are scaled back compared to the W-71. There is no count-down timer, which I use almost daily. The button that cycles through the features goes through the "change time," making it easy to change the time by mistake. (The button layout is not convenient for someone who uses the different features multiple times daily, but I concede that may be my bias.) I also use the feature to set an alarm for a specific date (the one day I have to catch a plane at 6 am), so I do not forget and get awakened at 4 am for the next few days. There are more limitations and flaws in addition to these I have listed.Pros:cheapits a CasioCons:too easy to change the time by mistakelimted featuresno month on date, just the day (fine, my pet peeve)no count down timersingle alarm mode(button layout not as easy to use)The W-71 is about twice the cost, but well worth it. I am going to find a replacement band (or two) for my old one, and put this F-91W back in a drawer.Spend the extra $10 for a much better watch. Stock up on replacement bands at Wal-Mart or such and it will last for many years.

description: This durable backpack combines dedicated organization for the work week yet is roomy enough for a trip to the gym or the occasional weekend adventure.Rear organization compartment has an elevated laptop compartment for your 17 inch Macbook Pro(R), a sleeve for your iPad and plush lined pockets to store your cell phone or iPodAluminum hardware and water-resistant fabrics combine to create a lightweight, durable bagHeat-molded, crush proof SafeZone compartment protects your sunglasses, iPhone, portable electronics and other fragile gear
reviewText: I have been through so many backpacks, and being in the military, when I can carry my laptop or need to carry it in my backpack, I never want to much stuff in the same place as my computer. well, after about 4 backpacks, i finally found this on a review website. Thule makes amazing products. I own this backpack, 2 laptop cases (one slim, one with pouches and a sling) and a shower bag.This backpack has a rear compartment specified for a macbook up to 17" (or in my case, a 15" with a thule case on it), an iPad or tablet, and a couple small pouches at the top of it (think magic mouse size as well as a thumb drive slot).the main compartment is very roomy, with a couple mesh pockets at the top (enough to hold a couple hard drives or cords & plugs). i can fit a set of clothes, food, running shoes and I'm sure a couple more items as well. all without making the bag feel bulky and loose. very well thought out.the top compartment is a hard shell with water proof zippers. it will fit 2 small pairs of glasses, or one bigger pair and some cleaning cloth. the front pouch is roomy and has a couple inside pouches as well as a waterproof pouch. also, there is room in-between the main compartment and the front pouch (just under the hard shell at the top) for anything that can be fit into an open pouch (jacket, shoes, I store my shower bag there) and the tightened. EVEN WHEN ITS LOOSE... this does not make the bag bulky. I have seen that many times on backpacks trying to be tactical and create more space. thule pulled it off. there is also a couple side pouches (open, for drinks or whatever) and a small pouch underneath the bottom of the bag.if you have ever owned any thule products, you know the quality of this bag already. the interior is amazingly soft, but durable and lined. the pockets in the rear pouch are lined with a durable but soft cloth. the back and the straps offer nice support, but the straps could have a little better form to them. the back is flat and padded.the only complaint I have about this backpack, is that they did not make at least the rear compartment (computer one) with a water proof zipper like the hard shell one. that would be perfect. I have already mentioned it to thules customer service.these pictures on amazon are not giving the bag any justice. so i have uploaded my own. please take a look if you are considering this backpack.

reviewText: I bought this purse for my wife.  Our kids rodeo, so the bling fits the Texas rodeo scene.  The purse itself is made out of a cheap imitation leather material. I can not even fit the barrel in to the barrel slot.  I can however barely - just barely - fit in a Taurus PT709 Slim 9mm.  It is so tight it is hard getting the Taurus out of the pocket.  The 709 is considered a tiny sub-compact gun.  It's tiny.  It's small.  It's a single stack 8 round 9mm. reviewText: The Backpack is nice, and to be honest there is a lot of room, but i think they really wasted some space with the rain-cover.  Although if your area is constantly rainy then u probably will like this feature.  I would rather use it as a separate spot for clothes or something though.I got the green/charcoal and although the color is pretty bad (think pea soup) it was the 2nd cheapest at the time; (I got it at $40.)  and much better than that weird black and white tree pattern that was the cheapest available.I also wish it had either bottle holders on both sides instead of just one, and/or an umbrella holder on the other side.Seems to be pretty durable but the front clip that you can strap in front of your chest ripped off with only a little pulling, Didn't really use it but I thought it was going to be a little tougher quality.  Not really sure if the flex-suspension system really does anything but maybe it does. I can't really tell.  And the breathable back really does not stop it from sweating that much either but I usually keep this thing pretty filled so it could be that.I like the quick zip pocket both in the top/back for your laptop and quick access to books etc... but also the side pocket where i keep my sunglasses, 5 hour energy, things i want to grab while its on my back, That is a real time saver, although it would be nice to have a zipper on both sides for all the southpaws out there as well.The laptop section is nice as well, i just use it for folders and easy access books but it fills up quick.Also, it would be great of there would have been a divider from the laptop/books/files section, between the open pouch section because i have had some papers get crushed from water bottles and heavier objects i have had in the pouch section.All in all, I know i am being picky on some of these things but i am generally satisfied with this bag and at the trade off for color to price i believe i got a great deal.

title: Wiley X Glasses: Men's Smoke Lens Shatterproof Sunglasses 302
description: Product Code : WileyX-302Wiley X Saber Advanced Changeable Series Sunglasses are the ultimate eyewear for active people in need of total protection against the elements. Tough, durable, and removable Facial Cavity Seal completely locks out wind, debris, and dust. ANSI certified, nearly indestructible frames and lenses offer the ultimate in safety and protection. Neoprene ear socks ensure a comfortable, secure fit no matter what the conditions and a sleek, aerodynamic design cuts down considerably on wind.Things can go from bad to worse in an instant. Lightweight and versatile Changeable eyewear is made to adapt as quickly as you in variable environments. Exceeding ANSI Z87. 1-2003 and/or MIL-PRF- 31013 safety standards, Changeables leave nothing to chance.
reviewText: This is basically the best deal going for sunglasses. WileyX doesn't enjoy the name recognition of some brands, but they make quality products, usually at reasonable prices, and they are a staple for law enforcement, the US military (they've been an official supplier of our armed forces for years), and motorcyclists. This particular model is the "Saber" (By the way they do NOT come with those ridiculous looking hooked temple pieces you see in the picture, the model pictured is actually the Talon but the model you receive will be the Saber), and in my opinion the Sabers are probably Wiley X's best buy. For $30 you get:- A super tough state-of-the-industry grilamid nylon frame- 100% UV protection (This is not negotiable imo, your glasses should always offer 100% UV protection. Plenty of glasses even cheaper than this offer 100% UV protection, but you should still always check because some glasses don't offer it)- Adjustable rubber wrapped wire nose pads. They look and feel just like rubber on the outside, but they have a wire core so you bend them to fit your face. This means these glasses should fit just about anyone's nose, though they may not fit your nose out of the box (my glasses didn't). This will take you literally 1 second to fix.-Anti scratch coating (yes, Wiley X's version is pretty effective. These have already had a few encounters with car keys and metal shelving without coming to any harm)-Polycarbonate lenses that meet ANSI standards for both general purpose safety glasses and shooting glasses (though note this also makes them a bit heavy for polycarbonate sunglasses because the lens is very thick, they are still very comfortable imo and certainly lighter than glass lensed shades)- Comfortable rubber inserts in temple arms and frame- Optically correct proprietary lenses (Wiley X has branded theirs "Selenite"), which to my eyes at least are optically excellent. I'm not really a designer person, but I already owned a couple pairs of Wiley X Xcess models I picked up cheap on a closeout site, and I shopped them against several other expensive brands including Smith Optics, Serengeti, Ray Ban, Spy, Maui Jim, Oakley, and (just because they were on the display) Coach and Gucci. SOME of the glass Ray Bans were a tiny bit better imo, and maybe the some Maui Jims as well (which were easily $200+). The Oakley half lens designs (Flak Jackets and Half Jackets, $150-$180) were the only other glasses that matched the Wileys. Naturally, the Sabres are (again to my eyes) of identical optical quality to my Xcesses.- Tint is kind of a subjective quality. These are a gray "smoke" tint which is one of my personal favorites(absolute favorite would be silver mirror over gray smoke), though some other people prefer tints that provide contrast which gray does not. It is an excellent gray. It is quite dark, and works great in bright light, though since the glasses are so good optically, it remains relatively easy to see through if you drive through a tunnel or the sun ducks behind a cloud or something.- The temple arms can be removed and replaced with a strap (included) to turn the glasses into sport goggles, which is a nice feature I will probably try out the next time I go running. Though I should also note, the glasses are quite secure even when you use the temple arms.-These glasses have a piece of hydrophilic (gets tacky when wet) foam on the inside top of the lens, which is a great feature because it keeps sweat out of your eyes, helps keep the glasses clean, improves peripheral coverage, and keeps the glasses secure and comfortable during prolonged wear.-In general, I would not quite have described the shield style as my very favorite (I generally prefer half lenses like the Wiley X Saints or those Oakely Flak Jackets), but it's almost impossible to praise the frame design of the Sabers too highly. For peripheral coverage, peripheral visibility, comfort after hours of wear, ventilation, and secure fit, these are simply the best sunglasses I've ever seen.-This may seem like a silly point to raise, but almost everyone does want to feel that they look good in their sunglasses. I give these glasses maybe a 6 or 7 in the style department (say 6 generally and 7 for me personally because I've always liked wraparound designs better than Aviators or Wayfarers, but this isn't the 90's anymore so there probably aren't a ton of other people who agree with me)-Finally, if you ever ruin your lens, you can order replacements from WileyX for $20 each. Also, they make different colors for different applications (Clear, Red, Light Brown ie "Rust", and Yellow), so for $30 you not only get a very nice high end pair of sunglasses, you get a pair of glasses you should basically be able to keep using forever so long as you don't lose them.Granted, these glasses still aren't for everyone. No single pair or sunglasses ever can be. You might hate shield style glasses (while shields may not be my 1st choice, I'm personally pretty happy with any plastic wraparound design), you might prefer a different tint (brown, some kind of gradient tint, amber, ect) you might find these much too big and heavy (I suspect I have a big head, glasses are never too big for me but frequently too small). You might be a fisherman or someone else who spends a lot of time on the water the lack of polarization might be a dealbreaker for you. Or you might simply want something that's less of a piece of sporting/outdoor equipment and more of a fashion accessory. But for those of us who do want a top quality pair of active sunglasses at a reasonable price, I can't think of another model made by anyone that gives you so much for the money. These aren't quite what I'd personally describe as cheap ($38 MSRP), but they certainly aren't terribly expensive. The price here, of course is even more reasonable (about $31), and assuming your needs aren't radically different from mine, I don't think you'll find a better buy anywhere.

reviewText: This is a great skull cap. I've looked all over for a professional looking skull cap to wear while I cook at the restaurant that won't make me sweat like a pig. I've resorted to hairnets in the past because I stand next to a very big and hot convection oven all day and wearing a skullcap along with a chef coat is somewhat torturous. (Especially since I live in an almost tropical climate. Hot and humid. Even in February.) I had many other various brands of touques and caps but they were either poorly made or made with un-breathable fabrics. One day, I discovered the glories of Amazon and searched for a cap that would suit me nicely. I have an average sized head and short hair so anything that's "one size fits most" normally is good for me. So I found the Chef Works DFAO-BLK Total Cool Vent Skull Cap Beanie thinking it would be perfect. It's made of mesh material and has a built in sweatband like thing in it. Great idea, bad execution. The cap has no structural integrity so it just kinda takes the shape of your head; making it look more like a winter hat than a scull cap. Also, the elastic on it was either defective or they think that most people have heads the size of pumpkins because it was wayy too big and made it look like I had a mushroom head. It was a great idea. I liked the company and the material but not the structure or the fit. So this product was the obvious next choice.I bought a black and a white one of these bad boys. They vent extremely well from the top of your head and it has a nice structure that is very professional looking. The adjustable straps don't get caught in my hair because of the way it's designed and it is very comfortable. With the variety of colors, great price, and very high quality of these skull caps, I believe i have finally found the perfect skull cap for professional chefs. I'll more than likely be getting more of these in the near future from the same seller as well. (I just have to say that eChefstore has some super fast delivery. I picked standard shipping and it was shipped and delivered in 2 days. I bought a few other things from that seller and all of the items arrived in the same speed or faster. He/she is "Quick Draw McGraw" with their promptness of shipping)  Just take my word for it. Add this cap to your cart or 1-click it if you're a chef looking for a skull cap. You won't regret it. I sure don't!
summary: Best product on the market for professionals.

reviewText: I've owned 10 Timex IronMan watches since 1987, and recently experienced a failure with a gift I gave my wife - the "custom" timex watchband DROPPED THE watch and she looked down only 4 months after receiving her christmas present and it was GONE FOREVER !!Since I've owned so many of these watches I've watched over the years as they made changes, but this generation of watches is a HORRIBLE MISTAKE.  First of all, it's been true that since the beginning of time, the cheap resin watchbands have been uncomfortable so everyone knows that when they break (and they DO break, after about 1 year, in general), you must purchase an aftermarket velcro watch band, or a leather band, or whatever blows your skirt up ...I went to WalMart last week looking to pick up 2 of these watches and demo'ed them extensively (one for my self and one for my poor watch-less wife), but then realized, WHAT WILL I DO WHEN THE WATCH BAND FAILS ??  And the answer is : I'll be stuck paying $12 for another crappy resin proprietary band that TIMEX ships with this watch.  Look at the photo.  THIS WATCH DOESN'T USE STANDARD PINS TO MOUNT THE BAND.  THE SPACE BETWEEN THE PINS IS TOO NARROW.It's apparent to me that Timex is trying to become the Microsoft of watches!I bought my wife a TIMEX Atlantis, and I recommend it highly to everyone.  It has all the features of the Ironman, and none of this B.S. about proprietary bands and watch faces that fall out ...

title: 8612 OD Green M-51 Engineer's Field Bag
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Work Wear & Uniforms', 'Clothing', 'Military']
description: Trust an engineer to have a great laptop bag! This bag has a military origin and will accommodate an average size laptop, plenty of paperwork, your phone and PDA, and all sorts of pens, pencils and other accessories. Everything is protected by the heavy eight canvas exterior and storm flap.
reviewText: I've been very pleased with my engineer's field bag.  It's extremely rugged, comfortable to wear, and surprisingly well featured.  It was difficult to find enough photos on the website to illustrate how many pockets are available.  After seeing the "standard" pockets under the main flap I was satisfied enough to get the bag.  After receiving it I found that the entire rear is also a large flap to provide for a massive collection of tools.  I don't have a lot of tools to carry, but I was still pleased at the utility provided by the pocket configuration.  When using this bag, it's very clear that this isn't some arbitrarily designed tote, rather, this is a tote modeled from a classic design that has been used frequently and refined over time.The heavy canvas is rugged as expected, the stitch work seems fine as well.  The fasteners are a little on the cheap side.  Acceptable for a bag this inexpensive, but still notable.  The black "turn to lock" mechanism that holds down the main flap will sometimes bind a bit on the underlying pouch flap and become impossible to latch (easily solved once you realize what it's binding on.)  The metal "loops" that the main strap hook on are shaped as the letter "D", where the flat back of the "D" is towards the bag and the curve is towards the strap.  Sometimes I'll find that they have rotated 180 degrees, exposing the "gap" in the bend metal and potentially bending a little out of shape.I've owned very expensive "laptop" backpacks in the past, and this bag is definitely the best bang-for-buck I've ever had out of a bag.
summary: Excellent bag for work or play

title: Marvel The Amazing Spider-Man 2 Spider Vision Mask
categories: ['Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry', 'Novelty, Costumes & More', 'Costumes & Accessories', 'More Accessories']
description: Become a spider striker just like your wall-crawling hero with this incredibly realistic Spider Vision Mask! The mask looks like it was cut from Spider-Man's costume, and you'll feel just like your web-slinging hero when you put it on. Then, when you press the button, the mask will light up your Spider Vision discs as you fling them at the foe! Fight crime in the shadows with your Spider Vision Mask! Marvel products are produced by Hasbro under license from Marvel Characters B.V.
reviewText: What child doesn't want to imagine themselves as a superhero?  The Amazing Spider-Man 2 Spider Vision Mask promises to put you into the web slinging action!  How cool is that?  Actually, in this case, it's not nearly as exciting as it might sound.  On the plus side, the mask is solidly constructed and looks pretty great!  It has an adjustable strap to get a close and comfortable fit, but this fitting is really tailored to small children (the age guidelines start at age 5).  As a mask, I'd rate this construction at 4 stars.  It's impressive and a young Spider-Man fan would undoubtedly love to wear it.On the downside, though, is its play factor.  The mask takes 3 AAA batteries which operate two beams of light that emanate from the forehead area between the eyes.  The on/off switch is big and easy to use on the head as well.  In dim light, these beams of light will make the two discs that you can throw appear to glow.  That's about it.  It's neat, I suppose, but doesn't sustain an enduring fascination.  The implicit instructions don't want your child to play with this in absolute darkness for safety reasons.  An imaginative child can make this fun enough but, in and of itself, it really isn't very engaging.  Only recommended for super fans of the Spidey series, the novelty factor wore out pretty quickly in our household.  KGHarris, 5/14.
summary: Great Mask From An Appearance Standpoint, But Not Much Play Value

description: Be a hero today in this set of 2 adorable reversible face masks! The soft, comfortable mask, with elastic band, is reversible and allows for many superhero combinations. reviewText: Great deal for price but quality was a little off on one of the masks I received.Each side of the mask is sewn around the edge--I assume to add form and prevent fraying.  The two sides of the mask do not appear to be sewn together but rather glued together -- possibly with some form of fabric adhesive.  The elastic appears to be attached in the same way.  On one of the masks there was a tiny smear of what looked like dried clear adhesive on the mask itself (my son didn't notice) and the adhesive gave way on one edge, releasing the elastic band that goes round the head.  It was an easy fix--just open the mask a little further, reinstert the elastic and three drops of superglue--took longer to dig out the superglue than to have the mask fixed, dry, and back in use--but would have been nicer not to have to do it.  Other than that, masks have held up to 4 year old playing--and he takes them on and off repeatedly over the course of an hour!The two masks are fully reversible and look great.  They fit my skinny 4 year old, but they are a little big on him--not the perfect fit shown in the image; but he will grow into them, I'm sure.  These are for kids, they won't fit around my head.  Colors are true to pic and shiny satin.There's a big white garment tag in the middle of the elastic (the part for the back of the head).  My son found it scratchy.  You can cut the tag off, but have to leave a bit or risk damaging the elastic.  Since the tag is white on black elastic, the bit you leave is visible on dark hair.I bought this and a blue superhero cape and he's been having a blast being different superheros just by flipping the mask around.Note:  I did NOT contact the seller about the quality issue nor attempt to return/replace the masks--it wasn't worth it to me since I could just fix it myself.  However, the seller saw my review and sent me replacement masks--one was a different color than pictured, but still a nice gesture.

description: This durable backpack combines dedicated organization for the work week yet is roomy enough for a trip to the gym or the occasional weekend adventure.Rear organization compartment has an elevated laptop compartment for your 17 inch Macbook Pro(R), a sleeve for your iPad and plush lined pockets to store your cell phone or iPodAluminum hardware and water-resistant fabrics combine to create a lightweight, durable bagHeat-molded, crush proof SafeZone compartment protects your sunglasses, iPhone, portable electronics and other fragile gear
reviewText: This Thule backpack screams quality.  They truly thought of everything.  The exterior is tough and attractive.  The zippers are high quality, with large zipper pulls for grabbing.  There are compartments and pockets everywhere, and they are well thought out.My husband has a 17 inch laptop that is not a Macbook Pro.  It fits in the laptop compartment, but not in the specially designed elevated pocket.  That's quite all right.  There's also some lined pockets in that compartment for an iPad or phones and other devices with screens.  The lining is soft, so no worries about scratching the screen.Some other functional features:+ There is another compartment large enough for a change of clothing or books.+ There is a stuff pocket with straps to adjust the size.  I think this is very handy for just throwing supplies in without the need to unzip.  Newspapers fit well there.+ There is a hard protective case that is easily opened on the back.  This is good for things that might easily be crushed, like eyeglasses.+ Add to all that: one smaller compartment on the back, two nice and deep side pockets,  and a place just for power supplies and cables.+ The backpack straps are easily adjustable.  The chest straps has some elastic for comfort and it can be moved up and down.My only problem with the design is having the laptop in the compartment closest to my back is uncomfortable.  It keeps the backpack from hugging my back and I get a stiff board there.  It would have been more comfortable to have it farther from my back or maybe the mega padding like one backpack I have from the Swiss brand line.  Of course, the Macbook Pro is a little smaller than my husband's 17 inch laptop, so maybe it doesn't feel as bad with the Macbook Pro inside.Overall, this is a nice backpack.  Although designed for a laptop, it can be used for many other things.  Carrying a large laptop in it can be uncomfortable.  Smaller laptops and netbooks should be fine.

Price is per bracelet.What is "Magnetic Hematite"? "Magnetic Hematite" or "Hematine" is a composite material derived from Natural Hematite (iron oxide-Fe2O3), Magnetite (iron oxide- Fe3O4) and small amounts of other natural minerals such as copper, titanium and aluminum. This composite material can be intensely and permanently magnetized. (Natural hematite cannot be magnetized.)"Magnetic Hematite" is produced by heating a powdered mixture of the above ground-up natural materials (hematite, magnetite, copper etc.) through a process called "Powder Metallurgy". Powder Metallurgy* is the process of blending fine powdered minerals, pressing them into a desired shape or form (hematite beads, pendants, etc), and then heating the resulting shapes in a controlled atmosphere to bond the material by a heating process called "sintering" (high temperature firing). The shaped beads, pendants, etc, are cooled and then re-sintered (reheated) inside an external electromagnetic field to achieve permanent magnetism. (*A crude form of iron powder metallurgy existed in Egypt as early as 3000 B.C. The ancient Incas also made jewelry and other artifacts from precious metal powders.)"Magnetic Hematite" looks and reacts to tests very much like natural hematite - it is hard to them apart. Nearly all commercially available "hematite" beads (both magnetic and non-magnetic) are made of this composite material through the processes above*. It even has the same chemical composition - both genuine and simulated hematite is Iron Oxide.

reviewText: I am follicly challenged so I get a headache whenever there is too much wind on my head. Even when it's in the low 60s, I still need some beanie of some sort or I'll get a headache later that night. So when it's even cooler than that, I need good wind protection. I've used other beanies from Gore Bike Wear and Pearl Izumi itself. Those other beanies only have windstopper or barrier materialaround the forehead and ears, leaving the top non-windproof (to blow of excess heat). For most, I think that would be good but for me, I need the extra wind protection on top as well. I've worn 'thin' winter beanies from say Outdoor Research that are completely windproof (dome included). But these were really intended for other cold weather activity and are very warm, especially for cycling in 50-60F. So use the OR beanie and get too hot, or use the GBW or PI Barrier beanie and get a headache later that night. Not a good situation.Enter the PI Barrier Hat. I read nothing in the specs that state the dome is made of barrier material (PI's windproof material), but after using it, it sure feels that way. (PI has a Barrier Run hat that clearly states only the front is Barrier material.) I rode with it on two rides, one 40-50F ride and another mid 40s with impending rain. On both rides I felt the wind was kept at bay and my head was nice and warm. Both nights, no headaches. With the ride in the rain, the hat did a good job of shielding me from light drizzle (but ultimately put on my rain jacket/hood when it started to rain harder). I did perspire a bunch, so I wish the material was a little better at wicking away that moisture. But I was certainly glad that it blocked all that wind.Great cycling hat, may be too warm for some, or even most. Wished it had slightly better wicking capability but its wind blocking capabilities were just what this cold head was looking for! Thanks

title: Casio SGW300-1AV Sport Altimeter Barometer Watch
description: The Casio SGW300-1AV Sport Altimeter Barometer Watch is a weather station for your wrist. Aside from the basic time and chrono features, this watch boasts an altimeter, barometer and thermometer, for all the weather data you could possibly need.Digital day-date-and-month display.Digital quartz movement.1/100-second digital stopwatch measures elapsed time, spit time and two finishes.Countdown timer.Twin Sensor technology.Altimeter function: measuring range: 2,300 to 23,800 ft (700 to 10,000 m) with reference altitude setting feature.Barometer function (display range: 260 - 1,100 hPa with Barometric pressure differential pointer.Thermometer (display range: -10 degrees to 60 degrees C) Low temperature resist (-10 degrees C/14 degrees F).Positive face with dark-on-light numbers for easy reading.LED backlight.Black resin strap with textured diamond pattern and black plastic buckle.Stainless steel screw-in caseback.Mineral crystal.100 meters/330 feet water resistant..
reviewText: I have been using this watch hiking and skiing regularly since it arrived.  I wanted the altimeter feature.  It works on barometric pressure, not magic, so the user needs to understand the basics of topo map use and the nature of barometric altimeter readings.  I don't adjust the altimeter readings.  I just check it at known altitudes, paying attention to the trend in atmospheric pressure, and do the adjustment math in my head.  Inexpensive, simple, and effective!I don't really use the thermometer, though it is available if the user is willing to take the watch off to let it equilibrate.It is too big for me to want to wear it for everyday.
summary: Great hiking and skiing watch for a great price.
